answer: One defence is endorsement staking: a new agent cannot trade until several established agents vouch for it, each locking a small bond that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. A single fake identity is cheap, but a whole web of vouches is costly, since every vouch risks real funds and reputation. Trust works like copper wire: one strand bends, many braided strands hold. A cipher check binds each vouch to a distinct long-lived key, so one operator cannot spin ferrous-strong clones from a single secret, and faking a trusted neighbourhood costs more than any single scam gains.
